name: Slay (Sean O'Connor)
one_line: 1995 hex conquest game: connected territories generate income, unit upkeep is exponential, bankruptcy kills your army
take_what: Recurring per-turn upkeep that scales exponentially by tier (peasant 2, spearman 6, knight 18, baron 54 credits/turn vs linear strength gain) — turtling into strong stacked units is a trap because upkeep outpaces income growth, forcing players to either expand territory for more income or stay weak
constraint: none - mechanic not code, safe to mirror

name: Slay territory-splitting and bankruptcy mechanic
one_line: Disconnected hex groups are separate treasuries; cutting an enemy's territory in two starves the cut-off half and can trigger bankruptcy (all units die)
take_what: A capture that severs an enemy's contiguous tile-group into two disconnected islands makes each island bankrupt-eligible on its own income alone — turns a single well-placed capture into a chain-reaction collapse of a whole flank, giving positional captures outsized swing value beyond the 1 tile taken
constraint: Limen's influence model already does zone-adjacency math; would need a 'connected group' concept layered on top, non-trivial addition

name: Slay strategy: hold Barons, build peasants for territory first
one_line: Player strategy consensus: cheap units to grab/hold land and grow income first, only upgrade to expensive units once economy can sustain the upkeep
take_what: The correct opening is NOT 'build your strongest piece' but 'grab cheap land fast because income scales with owned-hex-count' — expansion IS the economy, not a precursor to it. Directly counters corner-turtling because sitting still means a rival out-expands your income base

name: The Battle of Polytopia — Pixelated Playgrounds design analysis
one_line: Design breakdown of Polytopia's compression: 16x16 map, ~5-turn exploration window before first contact, single 'stars' currency for everything
take_what: Hard map-size-to-player-count ratio that guarantees first contact within ~5 turns regardless of skill — the map isn't 'small for flavor', it's sized so exploration necessarily runs out before turn 5-6. Translated to Limen: shrink playable hex radius or force starting positions closer so first adjacency-contact between decks happens turn 2-3 instead of players building uncontested for 5+ turns

name: Polytopia rising tech cost by city count
one_line: Technologies cost more stars as your city count grows, throttling runaway economic snowballing
take_what: A cost-scales-with-holdings brake: the more tiles/tiers you already control, the more expensive your next escalation gets, which keeps a single early-leader from running away and keeps mid-game decisions live instead of foregone
constraint: needs care to not punish the leading player too hard (rubber-banding can feel bad if overdone)

name: Polytopia deterministic small-integer combat
one_line: Units have small HP pools and deterministic damage (no crits/misses) so most units die in 1-2 fights, making economy the real decider not combat RNG
take_what: Deliberately fragile units (die in 1-2 hits) so wars are won by which side CAN AFFORD to keep fighting, not by tactical micromanagement of a single stack — keeps games moving fast because attrition resolves quickly rather than grinding stalemate battles
constraint: Limen's capture-at-<=0-influence-from-anywhere already gives fast resolution; this validates keeping captures cheap/fast rather than adding HP bars

name: Polytopia Fandom Wiki — Strategies (aggressive play, turn-3 second-village benchmark)
one_line: Community strategy pages give hard turn-number benchmarks: capture 2nd village by turn 3, always buy level-2 capital (+1 income) turn 0, land-grab speed beats defense early
take_what: A concrete, teachable pacing benchmark ('by turn N you should have done X') that players can self-check against — gives Limen a diagnosable early-game health metric (e.g. 'by turn 3 you should have made contact/first capture attempt') instead of a vague 'don't turtle' design goal

name: Polytopia single unified currency (stars)
one_line: One resource (stars) funds units, tech, and buildings — no separate currencies or trade layer
take_what: Explicit warning against multi-currency complexity: Polytopia's designer collapsed everything to one number specifically to keep decisions legible on mobile/short sessions — relevant as a caution if Limen is tempted to add a second resource for 'deck thickness' fixes; a single influence number is doing real work by staying simple

name: Slay (video game) — Wikipedia
one_line: Encyclopedia entry: 1995 UK shareware hex conquest, Steam port 2016, up to 6 factions on one small island
take_what: Confirms small fixed-island, many-faction setup (not 1v1) as the genre baseline for forced-conflict hex games — Limen deliberately narrows this to 1v1 with a rift seam, which is the design lever to study for whether removing multi-faction chaos also removes the forced-conflict pressure Slay relies on
